title: The threat you do not carry out
outcomes: Names the held threat in a position and the piece it ties down
Compares capturing at once with adding pressure first
Recognises a position where the capture should be made now, and one with no threat

steps.text:
A **held threat** is a capture or attack you could carry out but have not. While it hangs there, the opponent's pieces are tied to answering it. Carrying it out frees them.
So ask before every capture: do I gain something at once, or can I add pressure first? This lesson names the threat and the piece it ties down.

steps.caption: White to move. The knight on f3 attacks the bishop on e5, which only the queen defends.

line.say: Re1 takes nothing. It adds a second attacker against the bishop on e5.
Ng6 adds a defender, yet after Nxe5 Nxe5 f4 the knight is attacked twice, defended once.

claims.statement: Re1 is the engine's first choice.
Nxe5 at once is at least two pawns worse than Re1.
After Re1 two white pieces attack e5.
After Re1 only one black piece, the queen, defends e5.
After Ng6 two black pieces defend e5.
After Re1 Ng6 Nxe5 Nxe5 f4 two white pieces, the rook and the pawn, attack the knight on e5.
After Re1 Ng6 Nxe5 Nxe5 f4 only one black piece, the queen, defends the knight on e5.

steps.text:
**When to hold, when to cash in.** Hold when the capture only trades and a quiet move adds an attacker. Cash in when the capture gains material at once.
**Rule of thumb:** execute a threat only if something is gained immediately. A held threat is worth nothing if the target can simply move or be defended.

steps.title: Same knight, one change
steps.prompt: Decide for the side to move in each position: keep the threat in hand, capture now, or no threat at all. Predict, then check.
Before you saw the engine's answer on the silent items, did you decide to hold or to capture? Write which you chose and whether you checked how many pieces attacked and defended the target.
